analysis.title: CTA Update (Market Commentary, Not a Product of Research)
key_insights: Citi's CTA model signals CTAs to move to 'max short' SPX after the Nov 16 selloff, joining existing 'max short' positions in NDX and RTY. Their one remaining equity long is SX5E.
Citi estimates CTAs need to sell $15bn unlevered notional of equities over the next 5 sessions to add to existing shorts.

CTAs are signaled to halt SPX selling and move back to moderately short if SPX rallies above 7474 (+0.5% vs 7439 ESZ6). The NDX cover trigger is 28670 (+4.6% vs 27402 NQZ6) and the RTY trigger is 2856 (+4.2% vs 2742 RTYZ6).
CTAs hold a long in SX5E, but both signals to cut the long and flip short are within 15bps of the current level. The fund flips short below 6295 (VGZ6 ref 6302).
EM and Japanese equities are 'max short'. The furthest cover levels globally are 1654 in MXEF (+10.4% vs 1498 MESZ6) and 62719 in NKY (+6.5% vs 58900 NKZ6).
CTAs are back to 'max short' across the US Treasury curve after duration sold off last week following the higher-than-expected CPI report.
US Treasury cover levels are 102-04 in TU (ref 101-28), 106-05 in TY (ref 105-15) and 107-30 in WN (ref 106-18).
In Europe, CTAs are moderately short Bunds and BTPs and 'max short' Gilts and OATs. They add to Bund and BTP shorts below 121.62 (RXZ6 ref 122.06) and 112.39 (IKZ6 ref 112.65).
In Asia, JGBs are the CTAs' sole fixed income long. The flip-short level is 126.20 (JBZ6 ref 126.24), only just below the current level.
CTA commodity positioning is unchanged from last week: moderate long in Oil and 'max short' Gold and Silver.
Oil CTA signals sit within 6% of the current level: 80.95 to flip short (-6% vs 86.24 CLZ6) and 89.00 to move to 'max long' (+3.2%).
The first CTA buy levels in precious metals are far away: 4248 in Gold (+9.9% vs 3865 GCZ6) and 60.32 in Silver (+26.8% vs 47.57).
CTAs are 'max long' USD in all six FX pairs Citi tracks as the DXY extends to year-to-date highs.
The closest USD sell signals are USDJPY at 63.42 (JYZ6 ref 62.92) and GBPUSD at 133.84 (BPZ6 ref 131.90). The first EURUSD sell signal is much further, at 1.1385 (ECZ6 ref 1.0999).
Citi notes that many of this week's risk events are still ahead, and that 'max' regimes in its model do not mean positioning has reached a historical maximum.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The CPI report triggered last week's Treasury selloff, which pushed CTAs back to 'max short' duration. The report gives no figure.

risk_factors: Many of this week's risk events are still ahead, so the CTA signals could change quickly.
The SX5E long and the JGB long sit within about 15bps of their flip-short levels.
CTA positioning estimates are proprietary calculations and may not reflect actual CTA positioning or returns.
